subsystems.name: Manipulator arm
subsystems.role: moves the tool through space with repeatable accuracy.

subsystems.name: End effector
subsystems.role: the hand or tool that actually touches the workpiece.

subsystems.name: Perception
subsystems.role: lets the robot find parts that are not in exactly the same place every time.
parts: tactile or slip sensors in the gripper

subsystems.name: Motion control
subsystems.role: turns a target position into coordinated joint motion.

subsystems.name: Safety system
subsystems.role: keeps people and equipment safe while allowing close cooperation.

subsystems.name: Cell integration
subsystems.role: links the robot to the rest of the factory.

buildSteps.title: Study the task
buildSteps.detail: Measure the cycle time, part weight, reach needed and how much variation the process will tolerate.

buildSteps.title: Choose the machine
buildSteps.detail: Pick arm payload, reach and repeatability (often fractions of a millimetre) and a gripper that can hold the part without marking it.

buildSteps.title: Design the cell
buildSteps.detail: Lay out fixtures, part feeding, service access and safety zones, usually in simulation first so the arm can be checked for reach and collisions.

buildSteps.title: Install and wire
buildSteps.detail: Bolt the robot to a rigid base, dress the cables, and connect drives, sensors and the cell controller over a fieldbus.

buildSteps.title: Program the motion
buildSteps.detail: Teach key positions by hand-guiding, or generate paths offline from CAD; add vision and force feedback so the robot can correct for misalignment.

buildSteps.title: Train the perception
buildSteps.detail: Capture images of real parts under real lighting, label them, train a model to recognise and locate them, and test it against edge cases.

buildSteps.title: Validate safety
buildSteps.detail: Measure stopping distances and clamping forces, set speed and force limits, and verify every guard and interlock against the relevant standards.

buildSteps.title: Ramp up
buildSteps.detail: Run the cell at partial rate, watch rejects and takt time, tune, then hand it to production staff with documentation and training.

prerequisites.why: accurate, repeatable motion is the foundation of any automated task.
bin-picking and inspection need to locate parts that are not perfectly placed.
many assembly and finishing tasks require feeling contact, not just seeing it.
the flexible, general grasping that unstructured work demands is still mostly in research and pilots.
collaborative and high-speed robots can only share space with people under agreed rules.

pathway.milestone: fenced high-speed cells plus collaborative arms and mobile robots in logistics
pathway.unlocks: high-volume, repetitive work and warehouse transport.

pathway.milestone: robots that learn tasks from demonstration and adapt to part variation
pathway.unlocks: small-batch and mixed-model production that today is done by hand.

pathway.milestone: mobile manipulators that move between machines and load them unsupervised
pathway.unlocks: lights-out running of machining and inspection cells.

pathway.milestone: self-configuring cells that reprogram themselves from CAD and line data
pathway.unlocks: rapid changeover, so automation pays off even at low volumes.
